messages:
sophie: heads-up, seeing a spike of 5xxs from the new prompt routing endpoint (canary). traffic ~8% of prod, errors up to ~28% over the last 3m :rotating_light:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: PD#INC-9921 (on-call: @maria) — severity: P1 — Reason: prompt-route-canary 5xx-rate > 20%
maria: I'm on it, ping me any logs or a quick repro. @dan can you stand by to flip the flag if we confirm impact?
dan: standing by. linking the canary logs now — grabbing a tail from router-logs: prod-canary-1
sophie: pastes sample errors: ```2026-10-04T14:22:10Z ERROR prompt-router new-endpoint: upstream 502 Bad Gateway, id=abc123, prompt_id=xyz789
2026-10-04T14:22:11Z ERROR prompt-router new-endpoint: timeout writing to model backend, lat=1200ms
```
nicole: seeing corresponding SLO alerts in the console. latency p95 jumped from 180ms -> 520ms for canary requests. customer-impact: a subset of paid tenants hitting the canary route report degraded responses.
maria: thanks. assessment — canary is causing cascading 502s. mitigation plan: kill the feature flag to route all traffic back to stable endpoint, then monitor. I'll take control of the flag. @ops-bot please prep a rollback window?
ops-bot: rollback window created: 15m starting now. runbook: flip flag via admin API or console. Command: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/flags/route-to-new-endpoint/kill 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" 
 -d '{"state":"off","reason":"emergency canary 5xxs"}'
```
incident-bot: Action log: PD#INC-9921 — mitigation step: prepare FF kill. assigned to maria.
dan: executing kill now (curl from bastion) — pasted command output: ```{"status":"ok","flag":"route-to-new-endpoint","state":"off","changed_by":"dan","timestamp":"2026-10-04T14:26:02Z"}```
maria: confirmed via admin console that the flag is OFF. rolling routing back to stable endpoint. :thumbsup:
ryan: traffic fallback looks clean on gateway — error rate dropping in the canary pool from 28% -> 2% within 30s.
sophie: customer-support, can you surface which tenants saw failures so SRE/CS can notify?
customer-support: on it, pulling affected tenant IDs. preliminary list: tenant-42, tenant-88, tenant-acme-inc. will open support threads and notify impacted customers.
nicole: updating dashboards — overall platform SLOs trending back to normal. will keep 5m granularity for 30m.
maria: transitioning to post-incident: assign postmortem owner, collect logs, hold a quick sync in #inc-postmortems. I nominate @sophie for timeline and @dan for mitigation steps.
sophie: happy to own timeline. next steps: collect prom metrics (5m pre, during, post), router traces, and the canary deployment config. I'll start prepping a timeline doc.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollback event recorded: deploy/2026-10-04T14:20:00Z -> rollback to stable routing at 2026-10-04T14:26:02Z by dan
incident-bot: PD#INC-9921 status -> mitigated. on-call: @maria to follow up with postmortem.
maria: closing the pager for now. if the error resurfaces, I'll escalate to infra. great job team. :pray:
dan: note — the canary backend reported connection pool exhaustion under sustained burst. will open an infra ticket to investigate pool sizing and graceful failures.
sophie: adding that to the timeline. end of thread.
